questions.question: Which biome stores the largest amount of carbon on Earth?
questions.hint: The oceans are Earth's largest active carbon sink, absorbing vast amounts of carbon dioxide and storing carbon in seawater and marine organisms.

questions.question: Which bird migrates the greatest total distance each year?
questions.hint: The Arctic Tern travels up to 70,000–90,000 km (43,000–56,000 miles) annually between the Arctic and Antarctica.

questions.question: Which film became the first non-English language movie to win the Academy Award for Best Picture?
questions.hint: Released in 2019, Parasite made history as the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture.

questions.question: In the Star Wars saga, what is the birth name of Darth Vader?
questions.hint: Anakin Skywalker became Darth Vader after turning to the dark side.

questions.question: Which organization publishes the annual Corruption Perceptions Index?
questions.hint: The Corruption Perceptions Index ranks countries based on perceived public-sector corruption.

questions.question: Which international organization is responsible for global maritime safety standards?
questions.hint: The IMO develops international regulations for shipping safety, security, and environmental protection.

questions.question: Which emperor built the famous Colosseum in Rome?
questions.hint: Construction of the Colosseum began under Emperor Vespasian and was completed under his son Titus.

questions.question: Which document begins with the words, "We the People"?
questions.hint: The famous preamble of the U.S. Constitution starts with "We the People."

questions.question: Which country has hosted the Summer Olympic Games the greatest number of times?
questions.hint: The United States has hosted the Summer Olympics in St. Louis (1904), Los Angeles (1932, 1984, 2028), and Atlanta (1996).

questions.question: In golf, what is the maximum number of clubs a player may carry during a round under the Rules of Golf?
questions.hint: The Rules of Golf limit players to a maximum of 14 clubs during a round.

questions.question: Which country has the world's highest waterfall, Angel Falls?
questions.hint: Angel Falls drops 979 meters (3,212 feet), making it the tallest uninterrupted waterfall on Earth.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Europe and Africa?
questions.hint: The Mediterranean Sea separates southern Europe from northern Africa and has shaped civilizations for millennia.

questions.question: Which scientist first proposed the continental drift hypothesis?
questions.hint: In 1912, Alfred Wegener proposed that continents were once joined together before drifting apart.

questions.question: Which particle has no electric charge and interacts only through the weak force and gravity?
questions.hint: Neutrinos are electrically neutral, have an extremely small mass, and rarely interact with matter.

questions.question: Which civilization built the ancient city of Petra?
questions.hint: Petra, carved into rose-colored rock in present-day Jordan, was the capital of the Nabataean Kingdom.

questions.question: Which country is credited with inventing paper?
questions.hint: Paper is traditionally credited to Cai Lun of Han Dynasty China around AD 105, though earlier forms existed.

questions.question: Which insect species is responsible for pollinating the largest proportion of flowering crops worldwide?
questions.hint: Honey bees are among the most important pollinators for agriculture, contributing significantly to global food production.

questions.question: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
questions.hint: Canada's coastline stretches more than 240,000 kilometers (150,000 miles) across three oceans.

questions.question: Which law states that the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume at constant temperature?
questions.hint: Boyle's Law explains the inverse relationship between gas pressure and volume when temperature remains constant.

questions.question: Which civilization is credited with creating the first known alphabet?
questions.hint: The Phoenician alphabet became the foundation for many modern writing systems, including Greek and Latin.
